The oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) may be reduced by ethinyl estradiol, potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher likelihood of adverse effects associated with TCAs. 2. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of ramelteon by influencing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 3. Rosuvastatin may increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 4. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of topical ruxolitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction remains uncertain. 6. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of tizanidine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well understood. 7. Ethinyl estradiol and trazodone interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the oxidative metabolism of TCAs, leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of adverse effects. 9. Ethinyl estradiol and trimipramine interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 10. Acetazolamide may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 13. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Close monitoring is recommended. 16. Concomitant use of ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may result in additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ethinyl estradiol and amitriptyline interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 18. Estrogens and progestins may decrease the therapeutic effects of TCAs while increasing their plasma concentrations and associated adverse effects. 19. Amobarbital may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 20. Ethinyl estradiol and amoxapine interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 21. Amoxicillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Ampicillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The use of an alternative drug is recommended. 24. Anastrozole may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 25. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of antipyrine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Apalutamide may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 27. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels of bendamustine by inhibiting its metabolism. Bendamustine is metabolized to minimally active metabolites by CYP1A2, and ethinyl estradiol is a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Bosentan may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 29. Brigatinib may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 30. Butabarbital may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 31. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of caffeine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, potentially reducing their efficacy. The use of a non-oral contraceptive method is recommended for females of childbearing potential. 33. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 34. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime) may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Cenobamate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. 36. Ceritinib may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Chloramphenicol may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Cimetidine may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Ciprofloxacin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Clarithromycin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Ethinyl estradiol may also increase the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 41. Clindamycin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Clobazam may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods is recommended. 43. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of clomipramine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 44. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Conivaptan may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of an alternative drug is recommended. 46. Cyclophosphamide may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear.
